_doc: Assembler decisions for round 1, read by merge.py.

fact_edits: one entry for EVERY fact-level respect 'edit'. use = respect (apply the respect text: it only reorders, attributes, narrows, renames or removes, so the verified meaning is unchanged), verified (keep the verifier-supported text: the edit adds a claim the verifier never checked), drop (the respect pass found the verified text inaccurate or in breach of an ARCHITECTURE 9.1 rule, and its fix adds an unchecked claim, so neither version is double-checked; queued for round 2).
fact_drops: extra drops decided by the assembler (ARCHITECTURE 9.1 ranking of peoples, scope mismatch).
rank_allow: superlatives the ranking lint may pass because they describe a place, a tract of land, an organization, an agreement or antiquity, not the size or power of a people.

nations: one entry for EVERY nation-level respect 'edit' plus assembler fixes. Ops are applied after verify.names and respect structured fields, in this order: name, also, also_remove, also_add, also_search, lands, pronounce, official_url, name_source_url, new_id. A key that is present with null sets null.
url_map: exact URL rewrites applied to every URL field (only where the https page was confirmed live).

Round 2 (2026-10-10): gap-africa, gap-caribbean-guianas, gap-pacific, gap-south-asia folded in. region_map renames the workflow keys gap-* to published geographic keys (ARCHITECTURE 2.6); a nations entry may set 'region' for one nation. Four gap-africa lead names were flagged by the verifier as not shown on the cited name source: where a citable page fetched by the assembler shows the endonym it stays (Ishelhiyen, Britannica); otherwise the lead falls back to the exonym the cited page does show and the endonym is kept first in also, to be promoted when a source is found (Kabyles, Mozabite, Siwans). Sources: Wikipedia and Wikipedia imports (museum-digital actor text) were not used.
